Based on the screenshots and the reproduction, what’s happening is that when you supply a custom color and OpenLayers has to tint the sprite via an off‐screen canvas, we end up creating a “hi‐DPI” canvas (canvas.width/height = original×pixelRatio, with a `ctx.scale(pixelRatio, pixelRatio)` inside).  However, later in the Canvas renderer (in `CanvasImageBuilder.drawPoint` and `drawMultiPoint`), we pass the un-scaled `originX_`/`originY_` into the `DRAW_IMAGE` instruction, so on a retina (e.g. 2×) display it is cropping the wrong region of your sprite.

The fix is to multiply the offset/origin by the image’s pixel ratio when issuing the draw instruction.  Here are two *SEARCH/REPLACE* patches to apply to `src/ol/render/canvas/ImageBuilder.js`:

With those two changes, the sprite‐offset will be correctly multiplied by the DPR when drawing tinted icons, and your colored icons will line up exactly the same way on retina and non-retina screens.
